messages:
sara: Hey team — customer reported intermittent 400s from the /v1/embeddings route and lots of tail latency spikes. They say some requests return \"dimension mismatch\" even though their client uses the official SDK. Happening on prod (us-west-2) since ~01:30 UTC. Any quick ideas? :thinking:

leo: Can you paste the failing request body + the exact error? Dimension mismatch usually means payload shaping or a model variant mismatch. Also did anything change in batching config or model weights?

sara: Error payload: \"error: embeddings vector size 1535 != model.dim 1536\". Customer says 1536 historically. No cluster config change on our side. I grabbed a sample request they sent: `{"input": "...", "model":"text-embed-ada-002", "client_metadata": {}}` (they send batched arrays usually).

anya: ops-bot showed a kube deploy at 01:25 but that was a small infra patch (no model swap). Could be dynamic-batching interacting with max_batch_size when some clients send truncated arrays. Do we have a hook that strips trailing zeros?

leo: Not normally. Two immediate checks: 1) Is dynamic batching coalescing different client payload shapes into same batch and our pad/detect logic dropping an element? 2) Are any SDKs serializing floats in a way that loses the last element when compressed? Can you get the raw bytes for a failing request?

sara: Customer provided a hex dump of payload attached in support ticket. Quick reproduction I ran locally: 1) Use the SDK in chunked mode with many small requests 2) set max_batch_size=64 on route 3) send arrays of length 1536 but occasionally some libs produce 1535. Repro script: ```
# repro (bash)
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  python client_send.py --len 1536 --maybe-trim=0.005
done
```

leo: Nice repro. That \"maybe-trim\" is interesting. Could be client-side random trimming to simulate quantization tests? If client occasionally sends 1535, dynamic batching should detect and reject (400) but not silently coerce. Are we returning 400 or 500?

sara: Customer saw 400 with our dimension mismatch message, but the tail latency spike came from queuing while the batcher tried to reconcile different-length vectors. Queueing times increased ~600ms for some batches around the errors.

jamal: I pulled the batcher logs for that time window. There's an odd code path where when coalescing, we attempt to pad tensors at the last moment using a fast memmove path — that path assumed inputs are C-contiguous and missed the trailing element when alignment != 16. Looks like quantized uploads from that SDK produced non-contiguous buffers.

leo: Good find. So the pad routine can drop the last float if alignment differs. Two remediation steps: 1) patch pad logic to handle non-contiguous buffers (fix is small) 2) add a strict dim-check before enqueuing — reject requests that mismatch expected model.dim rather than letting batcher try to pad. Also add an alert when error-rate for embeddings.dims > 0.5% in 5m window.

ops-bot: deploy: starting canary rollout of emb-batcher-pad-fix to prod-us-west-2 (5% -> 20% -> 100%). Triggered by leo at 1765440005. :rocket:

anya: Also let's update our SDK docs and add a client-side validation warning. If some users mutate NumPy arrays in-place the buffer can become non-contiguous; recommend `.copy()` before send or use our SDK helper `to_contiguous()`.

leo: Patch landed in runtime repo. I'll also add an immediate config toggle: `enforce_strict_dim=true` for the embeddings route so any mismatched dim returns 400 quickly (reduces tail queuing). We can set that via the console and monitor rollout.

sara: After canary finished, customer confirmed errors stopped and p95 latency returned to normal. They pushed an SDK patch to ensure contiguous buffers too. Closing the support ticket but leaving follow-ups: update docs, add unit tests for pad alignment, add metric `embeddings.dim_mismatch_count` and alert rule. :white_check_mark:

leo: Addendum: created GH issue #4921 for the pad fix + test vectors. Will link to release notes.

sara: Thanks everyone, great triage. I'll file a postmortem blurb and include repro snippet and customer communication.
